title: Bernardo d'Alamanno de' Medici to Averardo de' Medici on the order to dismantle five castles, Lorenzana, 17 April 1432 (catalogue 2954)

documents.shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza V, doc. 196, c. 208r
documents.route: Bernardo d’Alamanno de’ Medici (Lorenzana) to Averardo de’ Medici

plaintext.source: No contemporary decipherment visible on the April leaf. The December letters carry interlinear glosses.

transcription.source: Codex from ASF image 415. All 339 cipher positions transcribed and aligned to the manuscript lines.

system.summary: One sign per letter, with multiple signs for several vowels. Names are spelled out.

diacritics.note: Shape and tail distinguish several signs.

system.sibling_key: Twenty values recovered by aligning the cipher with the interlinear gloss in MAP V, doc. 140, 8 December 1431.

prior_solution.where: Catalogue 2954 vetting and a follow-up search by sender, date and distinctive wording found no earlier decipherment of doc. 196. Checked again at the write-up, 24 Nov 2026: not among the 125 documents printed by Pellegrini (1889), who knew Bernardo's letters from Lorenzano; no match in the OCR texts of Guasti's Commissioni vol. 3, Fabroni or Ross. Kent (1978) not seen.

conditions.human_role: Andrew Aymeloglu requested the investigation and submission.

solution.what: Transcribe the April cipher runs and compare signs with the contemporary gloss on doc. 140.
Align doc. 140 with its gloss to recover 20 values covering 294 April positions.
Use recurrent spellings, place names and surrounding Italian to assign the five remaining values and read the April lines.

Apply the 20 values to two glossed passages of doc. 143. Word-aligned edit distance was 6 against 41 gloss letters. The best of 1,000 shuffled keys scored 23. The reader had seen this letter during selection.
Treating di on line 18 as cipher produced fi. The same di occurs in ordinary script on lines 13 and 15. The historical dictionary confirms the final word in a mio refe.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 339 tokens, 25 types, it-cinquecento order 4: reading -2.268 per letter; random keys -4.803 (z 6.5); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.025 (mean -3.088, z 15.1); annealer on the real text -2.671. Verdict: pass.

At the write-up (AI agent for the maintainers; not a person): recount and key replay (replay.py, docs/_replay.py). april.tsv has 61 groups of signs, 58 cipher words once the three words divided at a line end are joined; the two key tables give 56 of them as the edition has them and two with a letter supplied in brackets (Lore[n]zano, lasci[a]re); no unmarked difference; 339 of 339 signs exact.

At the write-up (AI agent for the maintainers; not a person): the 20 cipher stretches of transcription.tsv compared with the archive's image of c. 208r (1,272 px wide, the server's largest size, enlarged three to five times, no overlay). No differing sign found. Lorezano has eight signs and lascire seven on the image, so the two missing letters are in the letter as written. The di of line 18 is not settled by the image. Doubts listed in NOTES.md, Transcription doubts.

At the write-up (AI agent for the maintainers; not a person): on the archive's image of doc. 140 (c. 148), line 8, the word glossed above the signs D7o=8 looks like farlo, which would give D = f a gloss of December 1431. One look at a 1,272 px image; not confirmed, and december-key.tsv, april-key.tsv and the 294 and 45 counts are left as the contributor gave them.

At the write-up (AI agent for the maintainers; not a person): looked again for a printed text or decipherment of doc. 196. Pellegrini, Sulla repubblica fiorentina a tempo di Cosimo il Vecchio (1889): 125 numbered documents in the appendix, none of April 1432; no. 78 (Averardo, 11 Oct 1431) names the castles and says Bernardo was left there as commissioner, and a note to no. 82 mentions his letters from Lorenzano and the revolt of Chianni, taking him for Bernardo di Antonio. OCR texts of Guasti, Commissioni di Rinaldo degli Albizzi vol. 3, Fabroni, Magni Cosmi Medicei vita, and Ross, Lives of the early Medici: no match. Web searches by sender, place, date and wording: nothing. Kent, The Rise of the Medici (1978), not seen. None found.

Claims review of the page (AI agents for the maintainers; not a person): december-check.tsv read against the April values. The places printed ? in u?rra, bu?ha?no and conp?na are the signs E and G, glossed verra, bughagno and conpagna on doc. 143, so E = e and G = g have a gloss of 9 December 1431 if the labels name the same shapes in both letters (one reader, one label set). Three April values (2, D, f) rest on this letter alone. Key files and counts unchanged.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.268; polyphony 0.0; 0 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.671

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The interlinear decipherment is on the letter of 8 December 1431 (doc. 140) in the same filza. The April letter also supplied five sign values.
outcome.fraction_read_source: literal.tsv against reading-it.md, unit cipher words (words split across a line counted once: isfa-sciare, pietra-chassa, ra-chomandare): 56 of 58 cipher words read sign for sign; the other two carry a one-letter slip, marked in place (Lore[n]zano, lasci[a]re), and count as holes under the read rule. All 339 sign positions have a value (verify.py).

credits.note: Decipherment, transcription and translation with OpenAI Codex (GitHub pull request #778).
Interlinear gloss in MAP V, doc. 140, used to reconstruct twenty sign values.

texts.summary: Bernardo reports the order to dismantle five castles, questions whether Chianni can be relieved, and asks if the Ten intend the soldiers to plunder the inhabitants.
texts.note: The literal decryption covers only material in cipher. The Italian and English include the surrounding clear text of c. 208r. Editorial supplies and doubtful plain words are marked. read_share counts cipher words: 56 of 58 read sign for sign, the other two with a one-letter slip.

reading_review.by: integration review of PR #778 (AI agent, for the maintainers); not a person
reading_review.note: Grade given by the reviewer, not by the author of the reading: stated in the review of pull request #778 and entered here verbatim at the reviewer's request. reading-it.md was read as sentences against translation-en.md and the 20 cipher stretches of transcription.tsv were decoded by the reviewer's own decoder from december-key.tsv and april-key.tsv: they give the passages as read (the five castles, Chianni, Lajatico, Orciatico, Pietracassa, soldati mettano a sacchomanno, a mio refe, Antonio Mattaoni). The letter reads coherently; holes are single doubtful clear words ([?credo], [?tento], [?iscorio], [?Cirioni]) and two [...], none in cipher. About 58 cipher words, all decoded; two carry one-letter slips marked in place. Transcription not checked against the images (host unreachable). A model's reading: no person has checked it.

gaps.detail: ordinary script, not cipher; the readings fit the sense but the letter forms do not settle them

gaps.detail: ordinary script, not cipher; the tentative transcriptions do not give sense

gaps.item: line 18 di before the cipher resumes
gaps.detail: read as ordinary script (same d and i as la roba di, line 13, and di pocho utile, line 15); read as cipher the two signs would give fi

outcome.notes: Written up on 24 Nov 2026. Contributed by Andrew Aymeloglu with OpenAI Codex; the project checked it: key replay 56 of 58 cipher words exact and 2 marked, statistical validation pass, the cipher compared with the archive's image by an AI agent with no differing sign found. No person has checked the transcription or the reading. Five values (2, E, G, D, f) are in april-key.tsv and not in the doc. 140 table; E and G stand under the gloss of the 9 December letter (december-check.tsv), so three (2, D, f) rest on this letter alone, and D = f may have a gloss on doc. 140 (see the solution steps of 24 Nov 2026). No image is shown on the page: the Archivio di Stato di Firenze asks for a notice of every publication and the line 'su concessione del Ministero della cultura', and no notice has been given.
